Both are letters to the Secretary of Commerce establishing a temporary, sector-focused interagency committee; both identify Commerce leadership, specify participating departments and differing membership statuses, assign study and recommendation functions, and set a deadline tied to later governmental action. C18 and C17 share much of this committee-creation machinery, but C16 is closer in addressee, industry-policy setting, ad hoc participation, and overall operative sequence.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"I think an ad hoc committee, chaired by the Department of Commerce, would be appropriate.","parent_excerpt":"I am establishing a Cabinet Committee on Transport Policy and Organization... I am requesting you to serve as Chairman of this Cabinet Committee.","explanation":"Both establish a sector-specific interagency committee under the leadership of the Commerce Secretary or Department."},{"child_excerpt":"The committee should be composed of Assistant Secretaries or men of equivalent rank from the Departments of Agriculture, Commerce, Defense, Labor, State, and Treasury","parent_excerpt":"By copies of this letter, I am designating the Secretary of Defense and the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization to serve as the other members. The Secretary of the Treasury, the Postmaster General, the Secretary of Agriculture, and the Director of the Bureau of the Budget will participate on an ad hoc basis.","explanation":"Both prescribe multi-department membership and distinguish the committee's leadership from its other participating agencies."},{"child_excerpt":"Studies should be undertaken soon so that the committee could give its counsel to the Secretary of Commerce before the 1960 session of the Congress.","parent_excerpt":"I request that the Cabinet Committee on Transport Policy and Organization submit its recommendations to me not later than December 1, 1954.","explanation":"Both direct prompt study of an industry's problems and require advice or recommendations by a specified policy deadline."}]}
